key_insight: The paper shows that fault-tolerant quantum computers could simulate atomic nuclei using adapted nuclear Hamiltonians, with some shell-model cases reaching resource levels comparable to leading chemistry benchmarks.
engineering_relevance: It provides the first concrete Toffoli and qubit resource estimates for nuclear quantum simulation, helping engineers gauge when these problems may become practical on future fault-tolerant devices.
method: Build quantum algorithms for nuclear structure simulation.
Compile them for effective shell-model Hamiltonians and no-core-shell-model Hamiltonians with three-body chiral EFT interactions.
Estimate fault-tolerant resources in Toffoli gates and qubits for representative nuclei.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports resource estimates for nuclei such as 32Mg and 219At, and compares them against recent Femoco chemistry estimates while finding much larger costs for no-core-shell-model cases up to about 40Ca.
watch_item: No-core-shell-model simulations for light nuclei appear significantly more expensive, so practical implementation may require more specialized algorithmic strategies.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for simulating atomic nuclei
